report: An 80-year-old woman had progressive right upper limb weakness, gait disorder, neck pain and sensory loss with an osteolytic C3-7 mass compressing the cervical cord. Biopsy showed atypical vasoforming cells positive for ERG/CD31/CD34 and myo1B/CD146/SMA, Ki-67 10.6-16.1%, infiltrating muscle and fat; cultures and inflammatory/tumor markers were negative, refuting infection and non-neoplastic causes. Negative D2-40/CAMTA1/TFE3 excluded hemangioendothelioma and hemangioblastoma, leaving cervical spine angiosarcoma as the leading diagnosis.
